title: The plane quartic of Furio and Lombardo has exactly four rational points
description:
This is AI-generated research: the results, proofs and code were found and written by AI. Credit goes to all the humans whose work it builds on.

Furio and Lombardo (Proc. Lond. Math. Soc. 2026; arXiv:2507.17967) conjectured that the plane quartic curve $X_{E_3}$, a twist of the Klein quartic that arises in their classification of the $7$-adic images of Galois for elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$, has exactly four rational points. We prove this. A descent over a number field of degree $21$ lifts every rational point to one of two étale double covers of the curve. The Prym varieties of these covers are Jacobians of genus $2$ curves, and Stoll's Selmer group Chabauty at one $2$-adic place, applied to them, leaves only the four known points. The proof is formalized in Lean 4 with Mathlib. With the work of Furio and Lombardo, it completes the classification of the $7$-adic images.

The theorem is proved in Lean 4 with Mathlib, with no hypothesis and only the standard axioms; the Lean kernel checks every finite computation of the proof. The certificates it checks were written by PARI/GP scripts and Lean programs. A second program written separately in Sage recomputes the $2$-adic logarithms, the lattice, the centres and the boxes of the covering of the $2$-adic points of the curve, from the exact data and the local Selmer image of the first programs, and agrees with them; another Sage program redoes the descent and finds the same two classes.

Code, Lean proofs and certificates: github.com/mt0-svg/furio-lombardo-quartic
